{{Short description|none}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2019}} {{use American English|date=November 2020}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine | country = Maine | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine | next_year = 2024 | seats_for_election = All 2 Maine seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = November 8, 2022 | party1 = Democratic Party (US) | last_election1 = 2 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Republican Party (US) | last_election2 = 0 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_size = }} {{Elections in Maine}} The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the two [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Maine]], one from each of the state's two [[Maine's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2022|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. The elections will be conducted with [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked choice voting]], as per the result of [[2016 Maine Question 5|a referendum]] passed in 2016. These will be the first House of Representatives elections held in Maine following the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|2020 redistricting cycle]]. {{toclimit|2}} ==District 1== {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 Maine's 1st congressional district election | country = Maine | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine#District 1 | previous_year = 2020 | election_date = | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine#District 1 | next_year = 2024 | image_size = x150px | image1 = Chellie Pingree official photo (cropped).jpg | nominee1 = [[Chellie Pingree]] | party1 = Democratic Party (US) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = 3x4.svg | nominee2 = Ed Thelander | party2 = Republican Party (US) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Chellie Pingree]] | before_party = Democratic Party (US) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{see also|Maine's 1st congressional district}} Before redistricting, the 1st district encompassed the southern coastal area of the state, taking in [[Portland, Maine|Portland]], [[Augusta, Maine|Augusta]], [[Brunswick, Maine|Brunswick]] and [[Saco, Maine|Saco]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[Chellie Pingree]], who was re-elected with 62.2% of the vote in 2020.{{cite web |title=November 3, 2020 General Election
